reasoning_traces.think:
The second-order aversion primitive formalizes aversive motivation as a non-cyclical, externally gated process. It is derived from the observation that aversive behaviors are not spontaneous but emerge in response to specific threatening stimuli. This aligns with a threshold-based activation model where S(t) ≥ T triggers A(t). The non-cyclical nature implies no internal rhythm, unlike appetitive drives. The external stimulus trigger is the primary driver, not an intrinsic oscillator. In GSE, this translates into a deterministic transition from threat perception to aversive action. In GSI, it becomes a Bayesian model of threat likelihood conditioned on stimulus features. The failure mode arises when the threshold is misestimated or when stimuli are not properly categorized as threatening, leading to either false negatives or false positives in aversive response.
